sections.content:
109,240 people

were counted on the census as "construction operatives (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.

People who do this type of work may operate insulating equipment, fix plasterboard to ceilings and walls, help construct, maintain, repair and demolish buildings, clean and resurface eroded stonework, lay, join and examine pipe sections for drainage, gas, water or similar piping systems, install lighting systems in roads, domestic and commercial settings and carry out a variety of other construction operative tasks not elsewhere classified.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "construction operatives (other)" there were more men than women (96.7% compared with 3.3%).

This means "construction operatives (other)" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "process, plant and machine operatives".

Men made up 96.7% and women made up 3.3% of "construction operatives (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "construction operatives (other)" included:

  • rail and rolling stock builders and repairers
  • boat and ship builders and repairers
  • security system installers and repairers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "construction operatives (other)" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "construction operatives (other)", 14.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "construction operatives (other)" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "construction operatives (other)" included:

  • glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers
  • parking and civil enforcement occupations
  • electrical service and maintenance mechanics and repairers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "construction operatives (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of men than women with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "construction operatives (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "construction operatives (other)", 10.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (72.2% compared with 27.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (56.6%) than self-employed (43.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
